title: Console: color-contrast audit + in-app language switcher accessibility
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Scope: Run a focused color-contrast and keyboard-accessibility audit across three high-priority console surfaces: Dashboards (cost/cost-breakdown charts), Rollouts table (canary/A-B rows, status pills), and the global language switcher widget in the header. Goal is to fix failing WCAG AA contrast cases, ensure keyboard focus order and visible focus styles for dense tables and charts, and make the language switcher fully accessible and localized (labels, screen-reader announcements, numeric/currency formatting toggles). This ticket covers design decisions, accessible variants for dark/light themes, and deliverable specs for engineers plus QA test cases.
acceptance_criteria: All color pairs used in the three target surfaces meet WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text) in both light and dark themes as measured by axe-core/Contrast-Finder.

Keyboard navigation: header language switcher, dashboard controls (filters, date range), rollouts table cells, and pagination are reachable in a logical order with visible 2px minimum focus outlines across themes.
ARIA: charts expose data table summaries (aria-describedby) and interactive legend items are reachable and report state to screen readers.

Localization readiness: language switcher supports RTL toggling, numeric and currency formats follow locale rules, and no hard-coded text remains in components (design tokens for text direction/locale-aware spacing).
Design deliverables: Figma frames with accessible color tokens, annotated component variants (focus/hover/disabled/selected), and a short implementation checklist for engineering.
Automated tests: Storybook stories include an accessibility snapshot for primary components and an axe check in the CI pipeline for the three surfaces.
deliverables: Figma: Console A11Y / Intl - color-contrast and language-switcher frames (light+dark) with tokens
Component spec: focus styles, roles, aria attributes, and localization notes for header widget, rollout-row, and cost-chart legend
Annotated CSS token list (desired hex values, accessibility rationale, fallback tokens) for engineers
QA checklist and Cypress + axe test plan entries
engineering_notes: Prefer CSS custom properties for color tokens so engineers can swap values per-theme and per-locale in runtime.
Charts: use accessible-chart pattern (svg + <title>/<desc>) and provide non-visual alternatives via hidden data table and aria-controls linking.
Rollouts table: avoid using color alone to indicate status; include text and status icons with aria-labels. Ensure table row focus does not rely on :focus-visible only (some browsers differ).
Language switcher: keyboard activation should be Enter/Space; announce language change using live region and update html[lang] attribute on selection.
Engineering dependency: ENG-4124 (theme tokens refactor) must land before final token values are shipped.
testing_plan: Run axe-core automated scan on Storybook stories for header, dashboards, and rollouts after token changes.
Manual keyboard walkthrough: full header -> language switcher -> dashboard filters -> first chart legend -> rollouts table (row focus, expand actions) using NVDA and VoiceOver notes.
Contrast validation: run batch Contrast-Finder against exported theme palettes; save report under Confluence and attach to PR.
Localization smoke: test en-US, fr-FR, ja-JP, ar-SA (RTL) for layout regressions and numeric/currency formatting on Cost View.
Performance: ensure added focus outlines and aria attributes do not regress render times for large tables (10k rows virtualized).
